title: Majority-vote and self-certainty rewards, and where they collapse
brief: Build TTRL's majority-vote pseudo-reward and INTUITOR's self-certainty, train toy policies with each, and watch both lock in a wrong answer when the model's plurality or its confidence is wrong.
hints: np.unique(answers, return_counts=True) returns the values sorted, so np.argmax over the counts picks the smallest value among ties.
Reward accuracy compares two 0-1 arrays per sample: the pseudo-reward, and whether each answer equals the truth.
KL(U || p) = sum_j (1/V) log((1/V) / p_j) = -log V - mean_j log p_j. Compute log p_j as logits minus their log-sum-exp.
The gradient of log softmax(theta)[a] is onehot(a) - softmax(theta). Weight each sample's row by its advantage and average.
Use population standard deviation, np.std with its default ddof=0, and return zeros when it's zero: a group that all agrees carries no signal.
